common_name: Rio Verde Lablab (Texas A&M Wildlife Food Plot and Forage Hyacinth Bean)

planting.note: Direct sow 1-1.5 inches deep once soil has warmed well past last frost; Rio Verde flowers at an intermediate date between the early Highworth and the very late Rongai, giving it a wide practical planting window across the warm season.

directions: Rio Verde is a vigorous, twining Lablab purpureus selection released by the Texas Agricultural Experiment Station and named as one of the standard cultivars in the USDA NRCS Plant Guide for lablab, alongside Highworth and Rongai. It is grown across the southern and Gulf Coast states primarily as a warm-season wildlife food plot legume and grazing forage, prized for heavy, palatable biomass and pods that deer and livestock browse readily through summer and fall. Inoculate seed with a cowpea-type Rhizobium before direct sowing into warm, well-drained soil, and give the sprawling vines a fence, brush pile, or companion crop such as sorghum to climb for maximum yield. Once established it tolerates heat and moderate drought well, though like other lablab types it is frost-tender and is grown as a reseeding or replanted summer annual outside the warmest zones.
sources: USDA NRCS Plant Guide -- Lablab (Lablab purpureus)
